### Module(s)

mini.ai

### Question

Hello!

I'm trying to create a few custom text objects for Markdown files. I was hoping to use:
- `mb` for Markdown Bold
- `mi` for Markdown Italics
- `mc` for Markdown Code
- etc.

So if I have

```markdown
foo **bar** baz
```

I could do `dimb` to delete "bar".

I know I can create these with `gen_spec.pari()`, but the documentation says the mapping must be a single character. Is there any workaround for this?

Thanks!

Module(s)
mini.ai
Question
Hello!
I'm trying to create a few custom text objects for Markdown files. I was hoping to use:

mb for Markdown Bold
mi for Markdown Italics
mc for Markdown Code
etc.

So if I have
foo **bar** baz
I could do dimb to delete "bar".
I know I can create these with gen_spec.pari(), but the documentation says the mapping must be a single character. Is there any workaround for this?
Thanks!

comment_data.body:
Not through the `a`/`i` mappings. mini.ai reads the id with a single `getcharstr()`, so `m` is all it ever sees.

`custom_textobjects` is just a table lookup, though, and `MiniAi.select_textobject()` will take any key from it. So you can use multi-character keys there and add the `imb`/`amb` mappings yourself:

```lua
local ai = require('mini.ai')
ai.setup({
  custom_textobjects = {
    mb = { '%*%*().-()%*%*' },                  -- **bold**
    mi = { '%f[%*]%*()[^%*].-()%*%f[^%*]' },    -- *italic*
    mc = { '`()[^`]-()`' },                     -- `code`
  },
})

for _, ai_type in ipairs({ 'a', 'i' }) do
  for _, id in ipairs({ 'mb', 'mi', 'mc' }) do
    vim.keymap.set({ 'x', 'o' }, ai_type .. id, function() ai.select_textobject(ai_type, id) end)
  end
end
```

I tested it on `foo **bar** baz`: `dimb` gives `foo **** baz`, `damb` gives `foo  baz`, and `vimb`, `cimb` and `.` repeat all work. To keep this markdown-only, put the mappings in `after/ftplugin/markdown.lua` with `buffer = true`. The `custom_textobjects` entries can stay global, since they only fire through these mappings.

You could also make `m` a function that calls `vim.fn.getcharstr()` and returns the matching spec. That works for the first use, but `.` waits for you to press `b` again, so I'd go with the mappings.

When `mini.ai` runs an operation, for example with `dib`, does it essentially:
1. Note that the operation is `delete`
2. Visually select the region corresponding to `ib` (inside a block)
3. Send the `d` key to delete the selected text?

reply_data.body:
Close, but mini.ai never sends the `d`. In operator-pending mode the `i`/`a` maps just run `MiniAi.select_textobject()`, which enters Visual mode and selects the region. When the mapping returns with a Visual selection, Vim itself applies the pending operator to it. That's standard Vim behavior for omaps (`:h omap-info`). So yes, selecting the region is all a custom textobject has to do, which is why the `imb` maps work for any operator.

The one extra bit is that it passes along the operator-pending mode, so forced motions like `dVimb` (linewise) work, and it allows an empty selection for `c`/`d` only, so `cimb` on `****` still works.

comment_data.body:
Although using any fields in `config.custom_textobjects` (as suggested in [this comment](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/discussions/2574#discussioncomment-18802936)) may work, this is not guaranteed to be in the future (that's the reason I unmarked it as the answer). Textobject id is indeed only a single character by default, otherwise there is no good (robust yet not complex) way of knowing when to stop asking for user input.

There are several approaches that solve the original problem here:

1. The way I'd recommend approaching the problem of "textobjects for markdown" is through buffer-local config created for files with `markdown` filetype. This is such a useful and common approach, that [MiniMax has a dedicated example of it](https://github.com/nvim-mini/MiniMax/blob/14bd13f20268cc6c8464afedfbe4ab2430f9c353/configs/nvim-0.12/after/ftplugin/markdown.lua#L28). It is for mini.surround', but a similar approach is for 'mini.ai' textobjects:
    1.1. Create a `~/.config/nvim/after/ftplugin/markdown.lua` lua.
    1.2. Add (a variation of) [these lines](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/fa9037326e9996381e34a14b6350e18168618532/doc/mini-ai.txt#L510) to it. If using `*` and `_` is not mnemonic enough, I'd go with `B` for `bold`, `I` for `italic`, etc.

2. Use escaped variants of `<C-...>` keys in the global config instead of two-char ones (note that not all `<C-...>` will work, but it still something):

    ```lua
    local ai = require('mini.ai')
    ai.setup({
      custom_textobjects = {
        ['\2'] = ai.gen_spec.pair('*', '*', { type = 'greedy' }), -- <C-b>
        ['\t'] = ai.gen_spec.pair('_', '_', { type = 'greedy' }), -- <C-i>, a.k.a. <Tab>
      },
    })
    ```

3. Follow this part of [this comment](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/discussions/2574#discussioncomment-18802936):

    > You could also make `m` a function that calls `vim.fn.getcharstr()` and returns the matching spec. That works for the first use, but `.` waits for you to press `b` again, so I'd go with the mappings.

reply_data.body:
> I tried to use `balanced` but it doesn't allow more than one character. Is there any way to have separate patterns for bold (**TEXT**) and italics (_TEXT_) while using a balanced search?

The `type = 'balanced'` is described in the help as "Equivalent to using `%bxy` as first pattern". Lua's `%bxy` pattern, unfortunately, only allows a single character for both `x` and `y`.

The best suggestion for the behavior in markdown are present in the help and they prefer `type = 'greedy'`.

> If I wanted to make separate, manual keybinds for the `next` and `last` actions, is there a function that lets you select the next/last text-object regions?

[`MiniAi.select_textobject()`](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-ai.html#miniai.select_textobject) accepts the same `opts` as [`MiniAi.find_textobject()`](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-ai.html#miniai.find_textobject), which can accept `opts.search_method`. So to use a specific search method, the mapping RHS (right hand side) should use inside of it `MiniAi.select_textobject(..., { search_method = '...' })`.

Note, that there might still be shortcomings of creating manual mappings due to many small details in how mappings are used in Neovim. So the best suggestion still stands to not use manual mappings with "more-than-two-characters" ids, but follow the marked answer suggestions.

reply_data.body:
I finally did some reading about Lau patterns and the way `mini.ai` handles textobjects. I found that if binding to `MiniAi.select_textobject()`, empty objects get mutilated. For example if `_` is the cursor position, with 

```
_   **
```

and `cimi` (delete inside Markdown italics), you get

```
   *_
```

instead of

```
   *_*
```

i.e. the right-side `*` gets visually selected then deleted.

I ended up following your advice and using single-letter bindings. This is what I've got now (also showing `mini.surround`):

<sub>ftplugin/markdown.lua</sub>
```lua
-- custom text objects for Markdown
vim.b.miniai_config = {
    custom_textobjects = {
        i = { "%b**", "^.().-().$" }, -- *italic*
        b = { "%*%*().-()%*%*" },     -- **bold**
        c = { "%b``", "^.().-().$" }, -- `code`
        C = { "```().-()```" },       -- ```code```
        m = { "%b$$", "^.().*().$" }, -- $math$
        M = { "%$%$().-()%$%$" },     -- $$math$$
        h = { "==().*()==" },         -- ==highlight==
    },
}

-- custom surroundings for Markdown
vim.b.minisurround_config = {
    custom_surroundings = {
        i = { input = { "%b**", "^.().-().$" }, output = { left = '*', right = '*' } }, -- *italic*
        b = { input = { "%*%*().-()%*%*" }, output = { left = "**", right = "**" } },   -- **bold**
        c = { input = { "%b``", "^.().-().$" }, output = { left = '`', right = '`' } }, -- `code`
        C = { input = { "```().-()```" }, output = { left = "```", right = "```" } },   -- ```code```
        m = { input = { "%b$$", "^.().*().$" }, output = { left = '$', right = '$' } }, -- $math$
        M = { input = { "%$%$().-()%$%$" }, output = { left = "$$", right = "$$" } },   -- $$math$$
        h = { input = { "==().*()==" }, output = { left = "==", right = "==" } },       -- ==highlight==
    },
}
```

These work really well. Thank you for this amazing plugin ❤️, writing is fun now

This is because it is not possible in Neovim in general to visually select nothing. It is always at least a single cell.
